messages:
sasha: FYI we just saw ~150 ALB targets deregister in us-west-2 about 10m ago right after the CoreDNS config rollout. lots of 502/timeout healthcheck failures in the loadbalancer logs.

raj: ugh. which change was rolled? i saw a configmap apply earlier that tweaked upstream resolution/ttl.

sasha: yeah it was the split-horizon/endpoint-ttl tweak — rollout at 1951200000. snippet from ALB logs:
```
HealthCheck failed for target 10.0.2.15:80 - Timeout after 5s
HealthCheck failed for target 10.0.2.22:80 - Connection timed out
Target removed from target-group arn:aws:...:targetgroup/edge-svc-tg/abcd1234
```

emily: wait our TG is set to use the service DNS name for targets? i've mostly seen instance or ip target types. ALB resolving the service name + CoreDNS change + headless service behavior could be flipping endpoints under the ALB probe. ALB caches DNS resolution, but if it intermittently gets pod IPs that aren't reachable from the LB subnet, probes will fail.

kai: also saw some SNAT errors earlier but not matching timestamp. could be a race where ALB hits pod ips on the pod network and traffic never gets back. can someone confirm the target-type?

emily: checked console — target type is "ip" but we actually used a DNS alias pointing at the service FQDN in the target registration step (legacy terraform). so ALB is resolving the name and sometimes getting pod IPs depending on CoreDNS response.

raj: that matches. the new CoreDNS behavior returns A records for headless svc with round-robin pod IPs and lower TTL. before it returned node IPs via the externalTrafficPolicy annotation. the change was intended to reduce cache pressure but broke the legacy register-by-dns flow.

kai: mitigation options: 1) revert CoreDNS config (fast) 2) change TG registration to instance mode / register node IPs (needs infra deploy) 3) change service annotation to publish node IPs again (might be safer)

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-1189 - ALB target deregistration in us-west-2. Severity: High. Pager duty: oncall-eng.

raj: i'm on rollback. pushing previous config now.

sasha: thanks. i'm warming a script to re-register targets if needed but prefer to rely on AWS re-register once healthchecks pass.

raj: rolled back CoreDNS config at 1951234620. watching.

emily: seeing initial successful healthchecks returning 200s from edge-svc now. targets are re-registering.

kai: re-checking metrics: error rate dropped, ALB target count back to expected. good catch on the DNS interplay. we should add a note to infra playbook: avoid registering ALBs against service FQDNs with headless services or impl a validation that service resolves to node IPs only.

sasha: agreed. follow-up tasks: (1) patch terraform to register nodes instead of DNS names, (2) add a post-rollout smoke test for any CoreDNS change that validates LB healthchecks, (3) RFC for default headless dns behavior.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2025-1189 acknowledged -> resolved at 1951234702.

sasha: resolved for now, thanks team :thumbsup:
